question.text: A 55-year-old client with 10-year pre-retirement horizon should tilt toward:

answer.text: Gradual shift toward income and preservation (debt sleeves, dividend equity)

explanation.text: The Logic: Standard life-cycle investing aligns asset allocation with the investor's age, horizon, and need for income. A 55-year-old approaching retirement has a shorter remaining accumulation horizon and a growing need for capital preservation and current income. Best practice is therefore to gradually shift the mix away from pure growth equity toward income-generating fixed-income sleeves and dividend-paying equity, while still retaining enough equity to offset inflation over a 20+ year retirement. The Trap: 100% small-cap equity adds maximum volatility and drawdown risk precisely when the investor has least time to recover. 100% derivatives is speculative and inappropriate as a core retirement allocation. Gold-only abandons productive assets and provides no income. Note: The NISM-Series-XXI-A PMS Distributors workbook (Sep 2025) discusses age and horizon as inputs to risk profiling, and notes that fixed income suits retirees and conservative investors and that SAA/rebalancing align portfolios to goals, but does not lay out the specific 10-year pre-retirement glide-path framing used in this question. The framing above is general life-cycle-investing practice.
